title: After the Dilating Drops

patient.name: Mr Foo Jia Hao
patient.presenting_complaint: Just had both eyes dilated; vision is now blurry and he is worried because he drove to the clinic

history.hpc: Mr Foo has just been dilated for a fundus examination. His near vision is now blurry and he is light-sensitive. He says: 'Now everything blur and the light very glaring, but I drive here leh, how ah?' He is a delivery driver and drove himself. The PSA must give clear post-dilation safety advice and help him plan safe transport.
history.pmhx: Myopia. Otherwise well. No narrow-angle history.
history.social_hx: Delivery driver; drove his own van to the clinic today.

va.right: distance 6/9 but near now blurred post-dilation
va.left: distance 6/9 but near now blurred post-dilation

investigations.post_dilation_care: Provide post-dilation advice: blurred near vision and light sensitivity (photophobia) are expected and last about 4-6 hours. Advise NOT to drive while dilated, offer sunglasses/UV protectors, and consider fall/road-safety risks. Help the patient arrange alternative transport.
investigations.va_distance: Distance VA preserved; near vision blurred from dilation.

diagnosis: Expected post-dilation blurred near vision and photosensitivity in a patient who drove himself — the key issue is safe post-dilation advice and transport. The PSA competency is clear patient education on the effects/duration and ensuring he does not drive while dilated.

immediate: Explain that the blurred near vision and light sensitivity are expected effects of the dilating drops
Explain the effects usually last about 4-6 hours
Advise clearly that he should NOT drive while his vision is blurred and he is light-sensitive
Offer sunglasses/UV protectors to ease the glare
Help him arrange alternative transport (taxi/family) and a plan to collect his vehicle later
Advise care with steps/kerbs to avoid trips or falls while vision is affected
follow_up: Confirm the doctor has completed or will complete the fundus examination
Advise that vision should return to normal within a few hours
patient_education: Reassure him the blur and glare are temporary and normal after dilation
Stress not driving until vision is back to normal, for his and others' safety
Suggest sunglasses outdoors and taking care on stairs/roads
Advise arranging transport and collecting his van once the effects wear off

key_points: Identifies that the patient drove himself and is now dilated
Confirms the symptoms (blurred near vision, photophobia) are post-dilation
Checks there are no unexpected/severe symptoms (e.g., severe pain)
Acknowledges his concern about getting home
Confirms the expected post-dilation effects and their typical 4-6 hour duration
Assesses the road-safety and fall risk while dilated
Recognises the symptoms as expected dilation effects, not a complication
Understands dilation impairs near vision and increases glare
Knows driving while dilated is unsafe
Clearly advises against driving while dilated
Helps arrange alternative transport and vehicle collection
Offers sunglasses and safety advice for stairs/roads
Reassures the patient and documents the advice
